title: astegolimab: failed or shelved in COPD
body:
Company: Roche (Genentech)
Pathway: Anti-ST2 antibody: blocks IL-33 signalling
Status: Phase 3 ARNASA missed primary endpoint (phase 2b ALIENTO met it); Roche to discuss next steps with regulators
Reason: ARNASA (n=1,375): 14.5% numerical reduction in annualized exacerbations, not significant; ALIENTO (n=1,301): 15.4%, significant. Exacerbations lower than anticipated in both.
Side effects: No new safety signals.
Trials: ARNASA (phase 3), ALIENTO (phase 2b)
Sources:
- https://www.roche.com/media/releases/med-cor-2025-07-21 (2025-07-21, company): ARNASA (phase 3, n=1,375): 14.5% reduction in exacerbations, not significant; ALIENTO (phase 2b, n=1,301): 15.4%, significant; no new safety signals; Roche to discuss next steps with regulators.
- https://www.hcplive.com/view/genentech-roche-s-astegolimab-shows-mixed-data-for-copd (2025-07-21, news): ARNASA (phase 3, n=1,375): 14.5% reduction in exacerbations, not significant; ALIENTO (phase 2b, n=1,301): 15.4%, significant; no new safety signals; Roche to discuss next steps with regulators.

title: benralizumab (in COPD): failed or shelved in COPD
body:
Company: AstraZeneca
Pathway: IL-5 receptor alpha-directed cytolytic antibody: depletes eosinophils
Status: Phase 3 RESOLUTE (2025) missed its primary endpoint; AstraZeneca to analyse the full data
Reason: RESOLUTE (n=689, eosinophils >=300/uL, 3 or more exacerbations in the prior year): numerical improvement but no statistically significant reduction in exacerbations.
Side effects: Safety and tolerability consistent with the known profile.
Trials: RESOLUTE (phase 3)
Sources:

title: CHF6523: failed or shelved in COPD
body:
Company: not stated in sources
Pathway: PI3K delta inhibitor (inhaled)
Status: Early study: target engaged but no anti-inflammatory effect; authors conclude PI3K delta is not a suitable COPD pathway
Reason: 29.7% reduction in sputum PIP3 (target engagement) did not translate into any anti-inflammatory pharmacodynamic effect.
Side effects: Cough in 95.2% of patients, mostly mild to moderate, resolving within an hour of dosing.
Trials: NCT04032535 (crossover, n=44)
Sources:
- pmid:39427187 (2024-10-19, academic): Crossover study (n=44): 29.7% reduction in sputum PIP3 but no anti-inflammatory effect; cough in 95.2%; authors conclude PI3K delta is not a suitable COPD pathway.

title: icenticaftor (QBW251): failed or shelved in COPD
body:
Company: not stated in sources
Pathway: CFTR potentiator (oral): targets mucus accumulation
Status: Phase 2b: primary endpoint negative; later development: not stated in sources
Reason: No dose-response for trough FEV1 at week 12 (primary endpoint); some improvements at week 24 that the authors say must be interpreted with caution.
Side effects: All doses well tolerated.
Trials: NCT04072887 (phase 2b, n=974)
Sources:
- pmid:37411039 (2023-07-06, academic): Phase 2b (n=974): no dose-response for trough FEV1 at week 12 (primary endpoint negative); some week-24 improvements to be interpreted with caution; well tolerated.

title: itepekimab: failed or shelved in COPD
body:
Company: Sanofi and Regeneron
Pathway: Anti-IL-33 antibody
Status: Phase 3 mixed: AERIFY-1 met primary endpoint, AERIFY-2 did not; companies to discuss path forward with regulators
Reason: AERIFY-2 exacerbation reduction at week 52: 2% (every 2 weeks) and 12% (every 4 weeks), not significant; AERIFY-1: 27% and 21%, significant. Fewer exacerbations than anticipated reduced power.
Side effects: Adverse events comparable to placebo (AERIFY-1: 67% and 68% vs 68%; AERIFY-2: 64% and 71% vs 64%).
Trials: AERIFY-1 (phase 3), AERIFY-2 (phase 3)
Sources:
- https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1121404/000119312525131697/d947351dex993.htm (2025-05-30, regulatory_filing): AERIFY-1 met its primary endpoint (27% and 21% fewer exacerbations at week 52); AERIFY-2 did not (2% and 12%); adverse events comparable to placebo; companies to discuss path forward with regulators.
- https://www.ajmc.com/view/itepekimab-shows-mixed-results-in-phase-3-copd-trials (2025-07-09, news): AJMC report repeats the AERIFY-1 and AERIFY-2 results; Sanofi said the results merit further exploration; Regeneron remains committed to the broader programme.

title: ivacaftor (in COPD): failed or shelved in COPD
body:
Company: not stated in sources
Pathway: CFTR potentiator (oral)
Status: Phase 2 in COPD: no improvement; authors call for dose-finding studies
Reason: Did not improve sweat chloride, mucociliary clearance, lung function or symptoms over 12 weeks (n=40); drug exposure was lower than in cystic fibrosis.
Side effects: Most common adverse event on ivacaftor: diarrhea; adverse event rates similar to placebo.
Trials: NCT03085485 (phase 2, n=40)
Sources:
- pmid:39316773 (2024-09-24, academic): Phase 2 (n=40): no improvement in sweat chloride, mucociliary clearance, lung function or symptoms; diarrhea most common adverse event; exposure lower than in cystic fibrosis.
